newsitem.title: LATVIA: EXPORT CREDIT AGENCY TO BORROW $5 MLN LOCALLY.
newsitem.headline: EXPORT CREDIT AGENCY TO BORROW $5 MLN LOCALLY.

text.p: Latvia's export credit agency plans to raise five million dollars by taking a loan on the local market, the agency's president said on Thursday.
The agency said it has not yet started providing classical export credits but lends money to local firms to buy the necessary raw materials and machinery.
The agency said it needed more funds to expand its guarantee provision and export credit activities to reach the planned 15 million lats target of risk covered for 1998.
"We are currently in consultations with a number of big local financial institutions," Dainis Dille, president of the agency, told a news conference.
"The agency would prefer the loan in lats but we may have to opt for other currencies as the seven percent rate on the lat, which we are after, is not realistic at the moment," he added.

The agency, founded in 1995, expects its capital to be boosted this year to one million lats from 520,000 lats and the guarantee limit in the state budget to go up to five million lats from 500,000 lats.
"Our average projetcs range between 50,000 marks to 200,000 marks and cover timber processing, construction services and textile industry," Dille said.
